title: Test Regression and Root Cause Tracing
description: Detects patterns that indicate test regressions introduced by implementation changes: uncaught import errors, API surface breaks, missing dependency declarations, and logic drift. Source: mhattingpete/claude-skills-marketplace test-fixing skill, adapted for A-CyberSolutions TypeScript/Node stack.

rules.message: Direct .message access on caught error. Use errMessage(e) utility — raw Error.message fails on non-Error throws (strings, objects).
rules.remediation: Replace `err.message` with `errMessage(err)` from '../utils/errors'. This is the project standard, prevents TypeError on non-Error exceptions.

rules.message: Direct array[0] access without length guard. If array is empty, this produces undefined and causes downstream TypeError.
rules.remediation: Add length check: `if (arr.length > 0) { arr[0].x }` or use optional chaining with nullish: `arr[0]?.x ?? fallback`.

rules.message: Hardcoded long timeout detected. Long timeouts hide real failures and slow down test suites. Use Promise.race with explicit timeout and rejection.
rules.remediation: Replace with Promise.race([operation, new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('timeout')), N))]). Makes timeout observable.

rules.message: Barrel re-export or CommonJS require detected. These can cause circular dependency issues and make import tracing difficult during regression debugging.
rules.remediation: Use explicit named exports. If barrel is necessary, document the dependency order to prevent circular import regression.
